notes:
I couldn't write any notes this time. My first attempt to open the source pages was blocked: the tool said I had no research calls left for this turn. That means I haven't read anything from Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit), Precept Austin, NET Bible or the other sites you listed.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and leave out anything I couldn't find. Nothing has been found yet, so there's nothing I can honestly include. I've left the notes empty rather than fill them from memory.

When the tool is available again (please ask me to retry), here's my plan:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word's Psalm 104 page, then Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Barnes on Bible Hub or StudyLight, plus Precept Austin's Psalm 104 page.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** I'd check whether the sites show real differences. Likely places are:
   - v. 4, because Hebrews 1:7 quotes it about angels (for example, Gill against Reformed or Baptist writers on Ligonier, Monergism or Desiring God)
   - v. 30, "When You send Your Spirit": whether it's read as God's Spirit or as breath, and any Pentecostal or Wesleyan use of it
   - v. 35, the prayer against sinners
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible's translator notes, such as those on Leviathan in v. 26 and the "waters above" in v. 3
   - Bible Odyssey, on how Psalm 104 compares with the Egyptian Hymn to the Aten
   - Catholic and Orthodox use of v. 30 at Pentecost and of the psalm in Vespers (New Advent, Catholic.com, OCA)
   - Any prosperity-teaching use of vv. 14–15 or 28, but only if one of the approved sites actually discusses it
